name: Didaco
bio: Florentine actor whom Wilde met at Genoa on his journey from the Riviera to Gland in the early months of 1899, and with whom he spent three days. Wilde described him to Reginald Turner as 'a beautiful young actor, a Florentine, whom I wildly loved', bearing 'the strange name of Didaco' and 'the look of Romeo, without Romeo's sadness'. No surname, age, dates or further trace appear in the letter, and nothing else about him was found in the pages read.
bio_note: Everything known here comes from one paragraph of Wilde to Reginald Turner, postmark 20 March 1899, Complete Letters (2000), p. 1132 (PDF 1178, printed folio confirmed on the rendered page image). The letter runs over onto printed 1133 and ends there with no further mention of Didaco (PDF 1179, folio confirmed), so that paragraph is the whole record on this page-pair. Dates: none recorded. Searched so far: the whole OCR mirror of the Complete Letters (2000) for every occurrence of the name, plus the edition's General Index; Frankel, Oscar Wilde: The Unrepentant Years (2017), PDF, the fullest scholarly account of the exile years; McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008) and Murray, Bosie (2020), PDFs. Frankel retells the Genoa meeting at printed p. 248 (PDF 262), independently confirming Genoa rather than Naples, and gives no surname, age or dates. No birth or death date is recorded in any source consulted, and none is likely to be: the record preserves a first name (or a trade) in another man's correspondence and no surname to search by.
